quick_skim.title: Generalizable Multi-Agent Planning from Signal Temporal Logic Specifications via Diffusion
quick_skim.abstract: Multi-agent systems in the real-world (e.g., drone swarms, autonomous cars, warehouse robots) must satisfy rich, temporal tasks while avoiding collisions. Signal Temporal Logic (STL) elegantly encodes such objectives, but current STL planning methods face critical limitations. State-of-the-art optimization-based approaches can handle arbitrary STL specifications but struggle with scalability, becoming computationally impractical as the number of agents grows. Learning-based methods efficiently handle a large number of agents with rapid planning times but fare poorly when deployment-time objectives differ from those used during training, and do not support planning tasks that require different specifications to be ascribed to different agents (i.e., heterogeneity) or team-level specifications requiring coordination of multiple agents. This fundamental trade-off between generalizability and scalability presents a challenge for realizing multi-agent STL planning algorithms in practice. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a new diffusion method for multi-agent planning with STL specifications. Using a differentiable approximation of STL, we integrate the STL gradient in the denoising process, making our approach generalizable to novel formulas whose predicates are placed anywhere within the goal region covered during training, while achieving the same scalability as existing learning-based methods. Our method supports heterogeneous specifications, and by using diffusion models, naturally enhances plan diversity, thereby significantly reducing safety-related violations (e.g., collisions) among agents. A detailed evaluation study justifies the utility of STL-guided diffusion-based multi-agent planners for constructing generalizable, scalable, and diverse plans. Videos and code are available at https://www.jeappen.com/diff-ma-stl/ and https://github.com/jeappen/diff-ma-stl .

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Learned diffusion planner for multi-agent drone swarms from Signal Temporal Logic specifications, targeting scalability and deployment-time generalization. Applicable to encirclement-like multi-UAV tasks, though it does not use reinforcement learning and does not study pursuit-evasion games.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 面向无人机蜂群等多智能体系统，既要满足丰富时序任务又要避免碰撞，现有STL规划方法在规模或泛化上受限。该文提出扩散式多智能体规划方法，在训练后可快速处理大量智能体，并在部署阶段适应不同STL任务规约。实验表明相比优化方法扩展性更强、相比传统学习方法泛化性更好。该方法可用于多无人机协同围捕等带时序与空间约束的任务规划，但并非强化学习，也不针对追逃博弈。

quick_skim.title: Uncertainty-Driven Replay Memory for Reinforcement Learning
quick_skim.abstract: Uncertainty estimation provides promising capabilities for reinforcement learning (RL) agents. Notably, estimating uncertainty can reduce the training time and enable agents to obtain greater rewards over time by exploiting information related to whether an action would facilitate exploration of portions of an environment that are well-known versus those that are relatively unknown. In this work, we propose a novel formulation of the experience replay buffer commonly used in RL that we call uncertainty-driven replay memory (UDRM), which entails an update scheme for internally stored memories based on uncertainty estimates obtained by an RL model during training. In contrast to existing forms of RL, which typically use temporal difference error or the distribution of transitions to update the replay memory buffer and train RL controllers, our scheme biases the memory buffer to store more uncertain transitions that will improve an RL agent's generalization throughout training. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed uncertainty-aware replay buffer enables an RL agent to obtain higher rewards during training compared to other existing uncertainty-aware RL frameworks.
quick_skim.llm_evidence_en: General uncertainty-driven replay memory mechanism for RL that can improve sampling efficiency; usable inside single- and multi-UAV interception/encirclement DRL training pipelines
